name: La Albarrada
tagline: The riverfront promenade where Mompox meets the Magdalena
description: A cobblestone waterfront street lined with colonial facades, restaurants, and mototaxi stands facing the Magdalena river. This is where evening life concentrates, with locals and visitors watching sunset over the water and boats docking nearby. It is the most photographed stretch of town and the natural starting point for exploring on foot.
bestFor: sunset views, riverside dining, first-time visitors
pros: best sunset and river views in town
highest concentration of restaurants and bars
easy access to boat trips and tuktuks
cons: can get busy during Semana Santa and holidays
some noise from passing tuktuks in the evening

name: Centro Historico (Plaza de la Concepcion)
tagline: The heart of colonial Mompox, church squares and filigree workshops
description: The historic core clustered around Plaza de la Concepcion and Plaza de Santo Domingo, packed with whitewashed colonial houses, wrought-iron balconies, and the silver filigree workshops the town is famous for. Most of Mompox's hotels, cafes, and heritage sites sit within a short walk here, making it the most convenient and atmospheric base.
bestFor: sightseeing, shopping for filigree jewelry, staying central
pros: walkable to nearly everything in town
easy access to guesthouses and small hotels
cons: limited wifi even in central hotels
streets can feel deserted and hot at midday

name: Santa Barbara
tagline: Around Mompox's most iconic church, quieter and residential-leaning
description: The area surrounding the Iglesia de Santa Barbara, known for its distinctive yellow-and-white tower and riverside setting a few blocks south of the main plazas. It blends residential streets with a scattering of guesthouses and small eateries, offering a calmer alternative to the busier Albarrada while still being an easy walk from the center.
bestFor: quieter stays, photography, longer walks along the river edge
pros: home to Mompox's most iconic church
quieter than the main tourist strip
still close enough to walk everywhere
cons: less foot traffic means quieter streets after dark

name: Barrio Pueblo Nuevo (outer town)
tagline: Everyday residential Mompox beyond the tourist core
description: A working residential district on the edges of the historic center, where most Momposinos actually live, shop, and go about daily life away from tourist infrastructure. Streets here are simpler and less restored, with small tiendas, local eateries, and few concessions to visitors, offering a more authentic if far less polished slice of the town.
bestFor: experiencing local daily life, budget stays, longer-term visitors
cons: longer walk or tuktuk ride to the historic sites
very limited English and tourist services
